description: GIFMod is an open source framework for modelling the hydraulic and water quality performance of urban stormwater and agricultural green infrastructure practices under given weather scenarios. It covers practices such as infiltration basins, trenches and dry wells, pervious pavement and similar systems, which users build as conceptual models from blocks of surface water, streams, overland flow, saturated and unsaturated porous media and storage, with processes including evapotranspiration, flow through pipes and weirs, particle and colloid transport, contaminant build-up and user-defined reactions, and it offers deterministic and probabilistic inverse modelling to interpret field and laboratory data. It was developed by Arash Massoudieh and co-developers and is included in the US EPA Green Infrastructure Modeling Toolkit, which describes three levels of modelling: hydraulics, particle transport and constituent fate and transport. An installer is available for download from the GIFMod website, and the source code is published on GitHub under the MIT licence, free of charge. Caveats: the website's news dates from 2016 and the GitHub licence from 2020, so development appears inactive. It is useful for design and performance assessment of green-blue stormwater infrastructure in climate adaptation work; a related record is the EPA National Stormwater Calculator.
